title: Measure, estimate & calculate physical quantities & explore, critique & prove geometrical relationships in 2 and 3 dimensional space in the life and workplace of adult with increasing responsibilities

lessons.title: Measuring and estimating on the farm
lessons.html:
Units, accuracy and estimation

Supervisors measure and calculate every day: hectares to plant, litres of spray mix, tons of feed, the volume of a dam, the capacity of a silo. Mistakes can waste thousands of rand or harm crops and animals, so you must choose the right unit, measure accurately and check answers with an estimate.

SI units and conversions

QuantityUnits and conversions
Length1 km = 1 000 m; 1 m = 100 cm = 1 000 mm
Area1 ha = 10 000 m²; 1 km² = 100 ha
Volume1 m³ = 1 000 litres; 1 litre = 1 000 ml
Mass1 ton = 1 000 kg; 1 kg = 1 000 g
Rainfall / irrigation1 mm on 1 ha = 10 m³ = 10 000 litres

Estimation

Before calculating, estimate. A camp about 400 m by 250 m is about 10 ha (400 × 250 = 100 000 m²). If your calculator says 100 ha, you know you made an error. Estimation is also used when you cannot measure exactly, for example estimating the mass of a steer from a weigh band, or the yield of an orchard by counting fruit on sample trees.

Accuracy and error

Every measurement has some error. A tape stretched on a slope, a scale that is not zeroed or reading a measuring cylinder from above all give wrong readings. Use the right instrument, check calibration, and repeat important measurements. Round answers sensibly: a field area to two decimal places of a hectare, not to eight.

lessons.title: Calculating area, volume and rates
lessons.html:
Formulae for 2D and 3D shapes

Area formulae

  • Rectangle: length × breadth
  • Triangle: ½ × base × perpendicular height
  • Circle: π × r² (π ≈ 3,14)
  • Trapezium: ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height

Irregular fields can be divided into rectangles and triangles, worked out separately and added up. A centre pivot with a radius of 400 m irrigates about 3,14 × 400 × 400 = 502 400 m², or about 50,2 ha.

Volume formulae

  • Rectangular tank or trench: length × breadth × height
  • Cylinder (round tank, silo): π × r² × height
  • Cone (heap of grain): ⅓ × π × r² × height

Example: a round reservoir with a diameter of 10 m and a water depth of 2 m holds 3,14 × 5 × 5 × 2 = 157 m³, which is 157 000 litres.

Surface area

Surface area tells you how much material you need, for example paint for a tank or plastic for a tunnel. The curved surface of a cylinder is 2 × π × r × h.

Rates

Rates combine two quantities. A spray rate of 200 litres per hectare on 15 ha needs 3 000 litres of mix. A pump delivering 30 m³ per hour applies 1 mm on 1 ha (10 m³) every 20 minutes. Always write units in your working so you can check them.

Worked check

A trench silo is 30 m long, 6 m wide and 2,5 m high. Its volume is 30 × 6 × 2,5 = 450 m³. Estimate first: 30 × 6 is 180, and about 2,5 times that is roughly 450, so the answer is reasonable.

lessons.title: Geometrical relationships and proof
lessons.html:
Using geometry to solve and check problems

Pythagoras

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the longest side (hypotenuse) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: c² = a² + b². Farmers use the 3-4-5 rule to set out a square corner for a shed or a kraal: measure 3 m along one side, 4 m along the other, and adjust until the diagonal is exactly 5 m. Because 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5², the corner must be 90°.

Similar shapes and scale

Shapes that are similar have the same angles and their sides are in the same ratio. Farm maps and building plans use a scale, for example 1:10 000, where 1 cm on the map is 10 000 cm (100 m) on the ground. If the scale doubles the length, area grows four times and volume eight times. This is why a tank with double the diameter holds four times as much at the same height.

Critiquing a calculation

With more responsibility you must check other people's work. Ask: Are the units consistent? Is the formula correct for the shape? Does the answer agree with an estimate? Has a diameter been used where a radius was needed? These checks catch most mistakes before they cost money.

Proving a relationship

A proof shows that something is always true, not only in one example. For instance, you can show with the 3-4-5 rule that any triangle with sides in the ratio 3:4:5 has a right angle, because the sides satisfy Pythagoras.

Key points

  • 1 ha = 10 000 m², 1 m³ = 1 000 litres, and 1 mm on 1 ha = 10 m³.
  • Estimate before you calculate to catch errors.
  • Use the correct formula: circle area π r², cylinder volume π r² h.
  • The 3-4-5 rule uses Pythagoras to set out a right angle.
  • Doubling lengths multiplies area by four and volume by eight.
